summary: This bill requires the Secretary of Defense to issue rules mandating wellness checks for service members after significant injury, illness, or sick call, starting with electronic or phone contact and escalating to in-person if needed, with referrals for missing-person procedures if the member cannot be found, plus unit commander coordination with judge advocates, routine reviews of critical information requirements, confidential wellness meetings, and mandatory training on accountability.

scores.thoughts: The bill requires the Secretary of Defense to issue regulations and procedures for wellness checks and related training. This entails minor administrative implementation costs within the Department of Defense but does not address overall government spending levels, budgets, or fiscal policy in any substantive way.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, revenue collection, or tax policy.

The bill mandates wellness checks and accountability procedures for service members after injury or illness. While this occurs within the military healthcare system, it does not address broader questions of public/universal coverage versus private/market-based healthcare.
The bill has no provisions related to firearms, gun regulations, or gun rights.
The bill has no provisions related to immigration, border policy, or immigration pathways.
The bill has no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill establishes procedural requirements for wellness checks and training within the Armed Forces but does not alter military or defense spending levels.
The bill has no provisions related to environmental protections or regulations.
The bill has no provisions related to welfare programs, food stamps, or social safety net programs.
The bill has no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill has no provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or drug policy.
The bill references existing DoD procedures for classifying members as missing or AWOL when wellness checks fail, but it does not reform criminal justice, sentencing, or policing practices.
The bill has no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill has no provisions related to deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The bill has no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The bill has no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill has no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
The bill mentions electronic or telephone methods for wellness checks but does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or tech oversight.
The bill has no provisions related to unions, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
The bill has no provisions related to religious exemptions or civil rights protections.
